economist.name: The Economist
economist.notes: Senate+House model only (25,001 sims, polls from FiftyPlusOne). Senate seat counts in Economist files: dem_* includes independents caucusing with D (Osborn, Bengs, Achilles, Bodnar listed in independents.csv). Newsweek 2026-11-03 margins (NC +9, GA +7, NH +6, MN +4, ME/MI +3, OH <1; R: TX/KS <1, AK 1, IA 3, SC 4, NE 6, FL 8) are consistent with the data file. sin.name: Strength In Numbers (G. Elliott Morris)

racetothewh.name: Race to the WH (Logan Phillips)

Governor: only a mean count of D-held governorships (26.8 of 50) is published, no median. Wayback was unreachable from this environment for a cross-check. research.result: Scott Colom (D) 473,336 (49.19%) vs Cindy Hyde-Smith (R, inc.) 468,667 (48.71%), Ty Pinkins (I) 20,234 (2.10%). Colom ahead by about 4,700 votes (+0.48 pts) in unofficial returns. explanations.claim: The Black share of Mississippi's electorate was about 33% in 2026, up from 30% in 2024 (NYT estimates). Strength In Numbers calculates that with the 2024 electorate and this year's vote choices, Hyde-Smith would have won by about 4 points.
White Mississippians, who backed Trump by 67 points in 2024, voted far less Republican in 2026.
G. Elliott Morris attributes the Deep South Black turnout surge partly to backlash against Louisiana v. Callais and the redistricting it allowed, while saying the size of that effect can't be known.

Colom's lead grew after election night because he won a higher share of affidavit (provisional) ballots than of Election Day ballots, with large late gains from Hinds County (Jackson), where he took about 80%.
Before the election, the Secretary of State purged voter rolls using unverified Experian data. Inactivations doubled in some counties, which produced a large number of affidavit ballots.

Colom's 'pick another senator' ad, built on Hyde-Smith's 'so many proteins to choose from' remark about beef prices, went viral (15M+ views on X). After it, Senate Majority PAC invested $1.2M and later another $1M.

Political scientists quoted by Newsweek said the ad and the cost-of-living message helped at the margin. Brian Shoup (Mississippi State) said the midterm's turnout structure was 'the inverse' of past Mississippi races, with cost of living driving Democratic turnout and possibly depressing GOP turnout. Travis Ridout cautioned against crediting any single ad.

Colom's pollsters' formula was high Black turnout plus at least a quarter of the white vote. CNN describes Hyde-Smith as rarely seen during the campaign. Colom attacked Medicaid cuts in the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' that threaten rural hospitals, along with tariffs, gas prices and the Epstein files.

Candidate background: Hyde-Smith had blocked Colom's 2022 federal judicial nomination by withholding her blue slip. On election night she said 'I blocked Scott Colom from being a federal judge, and you blocked him from being a US senator.'

National Democrats engaged late: SMP began moving donors only after Labor Day. Warnock raised about $750K, Booker and other Black Democratic senators campaigned in October, Obama cut an ad, and Harris rallied for Colom on Oct 22. Trump held a rally for Hyde-Smith in Corinth in the final week.
Third party: independent Ty Pinkins (a former Democratic nominee) took 2.1%, which exceeds the final margin.
In the Voter Poll (exit poll), democracy ranked as Mississippi voters' second most important issue. Voters who named it the top issue went 66-34 for Colom.

Boebert, asked whether she blamed Trump: 'I don't blame any one person... We collectively failed. The American people let us know that we have failed in this governing experience for this Congress.'

research.result: Gina Hinojosa (D) 5,232,679 (52.82%) def. Greg Abbott (R, inc.) 4,525,947 (45.68%), Pat Dixon (L) 1.50%; margin D +7.1. Abbott conceded election night. First Democratic Texas governor since 1995.

explanations.claim: Final result Hinojosa 52.82, Abbott 45.68 (Wikipedia results box, unofficial).

The polling miss was huge: the final average had Abbott up ~3.5 and Hinojosa won by ~7, a miss of nearly 11 pts. ABC13 calls it the largest Texas statewide poll miss it could find, and the first since 2018 to run against the Republican. Turnout was nearly 10M, ~18% above the 2018 midterm record and 22% above 2022.

ABC News Texas Voter Poll (via ABC13): the GOP party-ID edge among actual voters fell to ~4 pts from 17-19 in the last two elections. Trump-2024 voters were 48% of the electorate vs 41% Harris voters, so persuasion as well as turnout; about 1 in 9 Trump voters backed Talarico. Latino voters (1/4 of electorate) went 66-32 for Talarico after splitting evenly in 2024 (Senate-race figures; governor similar).
CNN exit poll for the governor race: Latinos 24% of voters, Hinojosa 65-33; independents 59-38; moderates 67-31; 18-29 77-21; Trump approval 40/59; 10% of Trump-2024 voters backed Hinojosa.

Commentator (Texas A&M's Flora Charner): a surge in young and first-time Latino turnout drove flips; Rio Grande Valley swung back to Democrats; economy/costs top issue, ICE enforcement (incl. fatal shootings in Houston and Austin) a secondary driver.
Money favored Abbott heavily: Abbott raised $122.3M and spent $317.7M; Hinojosa raised $39.2M (Texas Ethics Commission via Wikipedia, as of Oct 24).

Campaign issues: Hinojosa ran on public education (ending vouchers and STAAR, firing TEA Commissioner Morath over district takeovers) and affordability ($1,500 household rebate); Abbott ran on property-tax elimination and border, and declined four debate invitations, the first no-debate governor race since 2010.

Late event: on the first day of early voting (Oct 19) Hinojosa sued to obtain Abbott-Elon Musk emails redacted as 'intimate and embarrassing'; a judge ruled for her Oct 26 and Abbott appealed. Musk had given $5M to Abbott.
Trump blamed Abbott: 'If Greg Abbott... hadn't become a RINO in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn't have lost.'
Dallas Morning News declined to endorse either candidate; Houston Chronicle, Express-News and Statesman endorsed Hinojosa.

research.result: Democrat Cindy Holscher, a state senator from Overland Park, beat Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson for the open governor's seat; Gov. Laura Kelly (D) was term-limited. With 98% of the vote counted, AP had Holscher at 552,328 (50.3%) and Masterson at 545,128 (49.7%), a margin of about 7,200 votes (0.6 points). AP called the race on Nov 12, 2026 (22:43 UTC); DDHQ had projected it earlier the same day. Holscher declared victory on Nov 4 and started transition work with Kelly. Masterson said he would wait for the statutory close-race audit and provisional ballots before conceding. I found no concession in the sources available. This is a Democratic hold, and it ends Kansas's roughly 60-year pattern of alternating the governor's party.
research.pres_2024: Trump carried Kansas by 16.1 points (R+16.1), per PollCheck's Kansas race page (https://www.pollcheck.co.uk/us-midterms-2026/governor/kansas). This is a statewide race, so no map change applies.

explanations.claim: Holscher ran a populist campaign: taking on corporate interests, fully funding special education, legalizing recreational marijuana, expanding Medicaid, and pausing new data centers. Masterson ran on capping property-tax growth at 3%, cutting spending, and a Mississippi-style literacy push.
Democrats tied Masterson to former Gov. Sam Brownback's tax experiment. One ad clips him saying 'the Brownback plan, which by the way, I wrote.' Masterson called the clip a 'lie'.
Masterson turned down two televised debates, so the Sept 12 State Fair debate was the only one.
In Emerson's September poll, Trump's job approval among Kansas likely voters was 40% approve, 53% disapprove, while outgoing Gov. Kelly's was 46% approve, 39% disapprove.

National Republican groups spent more than $10 million, much of it on ads attacking Holscher; the DGA spent nearly $4 million for her. Holscher outraised Masterson $2.34 million to about $2 million from late July to Oct 22.
The wave reached the whole Kansas ballot: Democrat Adam Hamilton beat Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in the same election.
Gov. Laura Kelly: 'Kansans have once again rejected a return to the failed policies of the Brownback era and chosen to keep our state moving forward.'
Holscher's closing pitch: voters 'want their leaders to put politics aside and work together' on public schools, lower costs for families and farmers, and the economy.

picked_winner.what: Holscher 48.2, Masterson 48.0, in effect a tie with Holscher barely ahead. Other averages favored Masterson: PollCheck by 1.2 and RealClearPolling by 1.8.

No rater or market favored Holscher. Cook moved the race to Toss-up on Oct 27 (no pick). Inside Elections had Tilt R and Sabato's Crystal Ball Lean R; MultiState's consensus was Tilt R. Polymarket had Masterson at about 70% and Kalshi had Republicans at about 70%.

research.summary: Holscher held the seat for Democrats in a Trump+16 state. She tied Masterson to the Brownback tax years, ran a populist economic campaign, and benefited from a national Democratic wave (Kelly was popular and Trump was underwater in Kansas). The final polls were split. Four late polls had Holscher ahead (AtlasIntel +4, WaPo/Schar +6, NYT/Siena +1, Survey 160 +1), while Emerson (+4) and CNN/SSRS (+5) had Masterson ahead. Most averages leaned slightly to Masterson. Ratings ran from Toss-up (Cook) to Lean R and markets gave Masterson about 70%. Only 270toWin's near-tied average had Holscher fractionally ahead.
research._notes: Our forecast gave Holscher 46%, so this was a mild upset. The AP figures and call time come from the brief; PollCheck/MultiState showed 551,243 to 543,599 (50.4-49.6) as of Nov 13, with DDHQ's projection at 3:01 pm ET on Nov 12. The Masterson concession status comes from Nov 6 reporting (KCTV5: he would wait for statutory verification and provisional ballots); I found no later concession. The four late polls come from aggregators (PollCheck, 270toWin, Ballotpedia), not the original releases. Ballotpedia credits the WaPo poll to George Mason/Braun Research in one row and to SSPG in another. PollCheck lists Survey 160 with several versions (49-48 LV, 49-47, 48-47 RV); the headline LV figure is used here. The Global Strategy Group poll for Holscher's campaign (Oct 18-21) was tied 47-47, so it is excluded. Final ratings come from Ballotpedia's table (Nov 3 column) and MultiState. The market figures are MultiState's pre-election snapshot. 'Democratic hold' is because Kelly is a Democrat.
